business_problem: NatWest Group wanted colleagues to get faster, more efficient support for workplace and HR queries while reducing the load on human support teams for routine questions.
solution_summary: NatWest Group deployed generative AI into its internal virtual colleague chatbot, Ask Archie, to improve how employees get support for workplace and HR questions. Ask Archie acts as the serving layer for a 24/7 conversational interface, while the Gen AI capability makes exchanges more natural and improves answer targeting for colleague questions. The implementation is grounded in NatWest's existing knowledge bases plus specific HR documents and policies, which function as the underlying information sources the chatbot surfaces to users. When a query is within scope, Archie returns targeted answers and links to the relevant policy content; when it cannot resolve a question, the workflow hands the case to a human colleague for further assistance. The initial rollout focuses on family-related HR policies such as adoption leave, partner leave, and shared parental leave, with NatWest planning to expand the knowledge coverage over time.

data_flow: NatWest colleagues submit workplace and HR questions to Ask Archie. The chatbot uses generative AI to conduct more natural conversations and draw on NatWest knowledge bases plus HR policy documents to return targeted answers and links to relevant content. If Archie cannot answer, the request is handed to a human colleague or agent for further support. The initial knowledge scope covers family-focused HR policies, with more content planned over time.
business_outcome: The Gen AI enhancement gives colleagues quicker, easier access to HR information through more natural conversations and more targeted answers, while allowing human agents to spend more time on complex support cases.
